chunks.text:
Bupropion is an antidepressant medication used to treat depression and seasonal affective disorder.
Bupropion also supports smoking cessation and weight management.
Bupropion is the active ingredient in Wellbutrin and Zyban.
Auvelity contains bupropion and dextromethorphan.
Contrave contains bupropion and naltrexone.
Bupropion improves mood regulation.
Bupropion improves nicotine cravings.
When combined with naltrexone, bupropion helps reduce food intake.
Bupropion is thought to work by changing levels of certain chemicals in the brain.
These chemicals include noradrenaline and dopamine.
Bupropion first became an FDA-approved medicine on 30 December 1985.

chunks.section_heading: What is bupropion used to treat?
chunks.text:
The brands of bupropion are FDA-approved for specific conditions.
Wellbutrin SR is used to treat major depressive disorder.
Wellbutrin XL is used to treat MDD and seasonal affective disorder (SAD).
Aplenzin is used to treat MDD and SAD.
Zyban (discontinued) was used to help stop smoking.
Auvelity (bupropion with dextromethorphan) is used to treat MDD in adults.
Contrave (bupropion and naltrexone) is used for weight management for specific patients.
The information on this page is only about bupropion.
It is not about bupropion with dextromethorphan (Auvelity).
It is not about bupropion with naltrexone (Contrave).

You should not take bupropion if you have an eating disorder.
You should not take bupropion if you suddenly stopped using alcohol.
You should not take bupropion if you suddenly stopped using seizure medication.
You should not take bupropion if you suddenly stopped using sedatives.
You should not take two medicines together that contain bupropion.
Wellbutrin is used for depression.
Contrave is used for weight control.
Aplenzin is used for depression.
If you take Wellbutrin for depression, you should not also take Contrave for weight control.
If you take Wellbutrin for depression, you should not also take Aplenzin for depression.
Do not use bupropion within 14 days before you have used a MAO inhibitor.
Do not use bupropion within 14 days after you have used a MAO inhibitor.
Examples of MAO inhibitors include isocarboxazid, linezolid, methylene blue injection, phenelzine, rasagiline, selegiline, and tranylcypromine.

You should call if you are thinking about harming or killing yourself.

chunks.section_heading: What other drugs will affect bupropion?
chunks.text:
You may have a higher risk of seizures if you use certain other medicines while taking bupropion.
Many drugs can interact with bupropion.
Tell your doctor about all medicines you use, and those you start or stop using during your treatment.
This includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Some examples of drugs that interact with bupropion are:
Digoxin: May decrease plasma digoxin levels.
Monitor digoxin levels
MAOIs: Increased risk of hypertensive reactions can occur when used concomitantly with Bupropion.
Drugs that lower seizure threshold: Dose bupropion with caution.
Medicines that are CYP2B6 inducers may require a dose increase if coadministered with other CYP2B6 inducers.
Examples of CYP2B6 inducers include ritonavir, lopinavir, efavirenz, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, and phenytoin.
Dose increases should be based on clinical response.
Dose increases should not exceed the maximum recommended dose.
Medicines that are CYP2B6 inhibitors may require dose adjustment if coadministered with CYP2B6 inhibitors.

chunks.section_heading: What other drugs will affect bupropion?
chunks.text:
Examples of CYP2B6 inhibitors include ticlopidine or clopidogrel.
Bupropion inhibits CYP2D6.
Bupropion can increase concentrations of antidepressants.
Examples of antidepressants include venlafaxine, nortriptyline, imipramine, desipramine, paroxetine, fluoxetine, and sertraline.
Bupropion can increase concentrations of antipsychotics.
Examples of antipsychotics include haloperidol, risperidone, and thioridazine.
Bupropion can increase concentrations of beta-blockers.
An example of a beta-blocker is metoprolol.
Bupropion can increase concentrations of Type 1C antiarrhythmics.
Examples of Type 1C antiarrhythmics include propafenone and flecainide.
These medicines are metabolized by CYP2D6.
A dose reduction of antidepressants may be considered when used with bupropion.
Dopaminergic drugs (levodopa and amantadine): CNS toxicity can occur when used concomitantly with Bupropion.
Not all possible interactions are listed in this medication guide.
